reference: AoU 6.1 (credits per RP and class); MAS 3.9; plan 3.15/12.14

description: Work conservation: a credit class does not stall for idle_cycles (crd_idle_cycles, default 4096) while an RP holds credit and work of that class at its AXI input; the DUT uses the credit it holds
With several RPs owed credit the DUT advertises them in header MsgCredit round robin: the first N grants name each of the N owed RPs once
The DUT never advertises more credit per RP and class than the MAS 3.9 maximum for that RP's RX FIFO depth and AXI data width, and once quiescent in ENABLED it has advertised exactly that
reference: MAS 3.4/3.9; integration guide 2 (FIFO depth parameters); plan 3.20/3.25

description: The credit the DUT holds for an RP covers every remote WriteReq/ReadReq whose AW/AR the M port has not taken, beyond a slack of messages past the RX FIFO (credit returns at RX FIFO dequeue)

RX flit framing: the DUT takes the header MsgCredit of every flit delivered to it once, in order, from bytes 128-129 (white-box tap of the RX core's MsgCredit output; a flit abandoned on LinkError may be taken)

Per-RP forward progress: no RP's messages of a class starve while the RP holds credit for them and is next in that class's order. Per local RP and credit class, the cycles the Adapter takes a beat on an open link and no M-port AW/W/AR or S-port R/B holds the DUT back, in which the RP has credit and work of the class at its AXI input (as T1-C01) and is next in order (write data: every write the DUT sent before the RP's oldest write still owing data has had all its WriteData sent; a WriteReq: no write the DUT sent still owes data, taken from the RTL), stay below starve_cycles (env cfg crd_starve_cycles or +crd_starve_cycles, default 500) between messages of the class on that RP; other cycles pause the count
reference: AoU v0.8 (forward progress); AoU 6.1 (credits per RP and class); MAS 3.2.1 (W follows the granted AW order); PR #98 (the aligner sends an AW with its first W beat)

description: A performance run measured every window it ran, and each gated link's steady state reached min_ss_flits

Each bandwidth window's link (l2r DUT TX, r2l DUT RX) delivers at least (1 - tol) x the d2d_model saturated bytes/cycle for the exact CONFIG, active PHY and traffic (tol 3% unless perf_overrides.yaml); a window link with no target or a target with no data is NO_TARGET

ABOVE_MAX: no link exceeds max(d2d_model value, the model's saturated packing of the messages the link carried in its steady state) by more than one flit of bytes over the steady state; above means fix the model once the measurement is confirmed
Over the whole window each data-path message type crosses each link in the share the d2d_model generator predicts (within max(1, 0.2%) messages)
ACTIVATE_START written while a deactivation completes leads to ENABLED again

The RX FIFOs (AOU_FIFO_RP) are on the core reset: at the release of AOU_SW_RESET none of them presents an entry (AW, W, AR, R or B, any RP), and no W beat pending at the release is handshaken on an M port afterwards (it would land under the subordinate's next AW)
With TIEL_DFT_MODESCAN=1 the core reset (w_DFTED_sw_resetn) stays de-asserted, AOU_SW_RESET written or not

With TIEL_DFT_MODESCAN=1 the SFRs keep their values and an AOU_SW_RESET write resets nothing (the software reset path is neutralised); a write made in scan mode stays pending and resets the core when TIEL_DFT_MODESCAN falls
AOU_SW_RESET puts the DUT core in reset (core_rst_n low) within 10000 core cycles of the write, so sw_reset() can flush the env at that edge
Local requests issued while DISABLED activate the link (MAS 7.3.5 INT_ACTIVATE_START)
The DUT sends no ActivateReq while more than a slack of remote WriteReq/ReadReq per RP still wait for its M port (the RX FIFO is emptied before activation)
ACTIVATE_START written while the FDI link is down reads back 1 with the DUT still DISABLED (read-back in the test; activation after link-up is T1-V02/T1-V03)
INT_DEACTIVATE_PROPERTY reads 0 in ENABLED and while in DEACTIVATE after a remote DeactivateReq with PropertyReq 0 (v0.8 makes PropertyReq RsvdZero, so a v0.8 remote die never sets the bit)
reference: MAS software-operation 7.1 AOU_INIT.INT_DEACTIVATE_PROPERTY; csr/aou-core.rdl AOU_INIT; plan 2.10

description: A DeactivateReq (PropertyReq 0) comes at least 2^(DEACTIVATE_TIME_OUT_VALUE+3) cycles (less a TX pipeline slack) after the DUT's last credited message
ACTIVATE_STATE_DISABLED within 8 cycles of INT_FDI_LINK_DOWN: the DUT disables itself on an FDI link loss with AoU in use, no handshake (the link is down)

An Adapter LinkError, LinkReset or Disabled that finds the DUT in ACTIVATE, ENABLED or DEACTIVATE raises INT_FDI_LINK_DOWN exactly once (0..1 when it finds it DISABLED); Retrain, L1 and deactivation raise nothing; write 1 clears it; with INT_FDI_LINK_DOWN_MASK set the pin stays low and AOU_INIT.INT_FDI_LINK_DOWN still reads 1

ACTIVATE_START written with the FDI link in L1 or Retrain: no INT_FDI_LINK_DOWN, the link stays where it is (L1 is left by the Adapter's PM exit, not by the write), and the activation completes once the link is Active again; local AXI traffic in L1 with ACTIVATE_START clear wakes the link (INT_ACTIVATE_START is an activation request) and its activation completes

INT_FDI_LINK_DOWN after an Adapter LinkReset/Disabled/LinkError or I_SW_LINKERROR_INJECT iff the AoU core was out of DISABLED (ACTIVATE with its ActivateReq unanswered); the core is DISABLED afterwards; write 1 clears the bit and the pin falls

A DUT DeactivateReq follows a DEACTIVATE_FORCE write made while ENABLED or DEACTIVATE within a fixed bound (4 PCLK + 256 core cycles; taken from the RTL path with margin, the force being implementation-defined); nothing after it is checked
With TX_LP_MODE=0 the DUT keeps sending flits in an idle window (at least window/16)
With TX_LP_MODE=1 and threshold 0 the DUT sends at most 4 flits in an idle window
AOU_CON0.TX_LP_MODE and TX_LP_MODE_THRESHOLD change only while the DUT reports ACTIVATE_STATE_DISABLED (static configuration; a change on a live link may land mid-flit)
reference: MAS software-operation 7.1 Low Power mode; project ruling: LP mode is programmed before activation or between sessions

description: Each remote-initiated activation is serviced once as INT_ACTIVATE_START
A remote-initiated deactivation is serviced once as INT_DEACTIVATE_START
A WriteResp the DUT sends matches a remote write outstanding on its RP and ID (late answers to aborted writes excepted)
ReadData the DUT sends matches a remote read outstanding on its RP and ID (late answers to aborted reads excepted)
A remote read gets no more ReadData beats than ARLEN+1
ReadData LAST is set on the last beat of a remote read and no other
No remote write or read is outstanding at the end of the test
A WriteResp/ReadData the DUT sends carries an RP below the remote managers' plane count
Every WriteData beat of one write burst carries the same DLENGTH
WriteData DLENGTH is at least max(the size of its WriteReq, 256 bits)
reference: AoU 5.4 (DLENGTH); project ruling: DLENGTH is self-describing, any width at or above the WriteReq's size is legal

description: The remote model's maximum burst length changes only while it has no request in hand
reference: project ruling: a maximum burst change is legal only while the remote is idle
